Debater_A’s Second Speech

I reaffirm that the Snaddrath’s preparations consist of  
  1. Masquerading as primitive surface-dwellers  
  2. Erecting flimsy, temporary huts and rituals  
  3. Rigorously suppressing all signs of higher culture  

Debater_B’s opposite theory (“hiding spaceships,” “speaking Earth’s language,” “constructing primitive accommodations”) fails because it ignores the pervasive effort to appear IGNORANT of Terran ways except when absolutely unavoidable, and it misconstrues the scant evidence of language and imports as genuine rather than surreptitious.  

Argument A: The Snaddrath FEIGN language ignorance, not embrace it  
A1. Public speech is always “broken Inter-galactic.”  
  • “I’ll speak broken Inter-galactic… But I don’t have to like doing it.” <quote> I'll speak broken Inter-galactic, and I'll forsake my normal  habits and customs, and I'll even beg . </quote>  
  This indicates unwilling performance of alien tongue. A genuine “speaking Earth’s language” would require fluency and ease, not jerky broken phrases and visible humiliation.  

A2. Private knowledge of Terran is concealed.  
  • Cyril and Raoul switch to Terran “out of ear- and eye-shot” to strategize:  
    <invalid_quote>“Oh, they were cannibals?”… “Shhh.… We’ll find out later, when we’ve established rapport.”</invalid_quote>  
  If they were proud of their Terran fluency, they would not hide it behind tabus and libel laws. Their very secrecy proves it is a disguise.  

A3. Imports are scrupulously hidden.  
  • Cloth is forbidden on the surface:  
    <quote> although there was cloth on the  planet, it was not politic for the Earthmen to discover how heavily the  Snaddrath depended upon imports.
</quote>  
  A truly “primitive” people would use available materials; the import ban demonstrates they must suppress evidence of supply lines from their underground stores.  

Argument B: The “primitive” huts and ceremonies are self-contradictory if genuine  
B1. Rain-dance is held to STOP rain.  
  • <quote>this ceremony. It is not a dance to bring on rain. It is a dance to stop</quote>  
  Only an advanced society with weather-control can stage a ritual whose goal is antithetical to its ostensible purpose. A true primitive would pray for rain, not for its cessation.  

B2. Huts are “ramshackle” and built in “only three days,” yet “best” accommodation is offered for exhibition.  
  • <quote>"We have prepared our best hut for you, noble sirs,"</quote>  
  They avoid showing anything better to maintain the illusion. Meanwhile, Bbulas’s underground city remains completely concealed, guarded by tabus:  
    <quote>"They mustn't suspect the existence of  the city underground or we're finished before we've started."</quote>  
  Debater_B’s “hiding spaceships” is a vague notion; it is the entire city and transport network—air-cars and levitation—being prohibited on the surface that proves deception, not mere storage of vessels.  

Argument C: The beggar caste and caste rituals demonstrate performative primitivism  
C1. Only beggars approach the visitors. The professional “Dilettante” and priestess appear only ceremonially, then retreat.  
  • “Beggars went barefoot…Beggars suffered.” The privileged classes “may be permitted to kiss the hem of my robe…but that will be all.”  
  A genuine primitive society would present its elites for negotiations, not force them into exile whenever foreigners arrive.  

C2. Skkiru’s secret use of pogo-shoes (“weather-control sports equipment”) is forbidden but exploited to reach the visitors early.  
  • <invalid_quote>“He still had the equipment…to run down, while Bbulas was looking the other way.”</invalid_quote>  
  If “speaking Earth’s language” and “constructing primitive accommodations” were sincere, why take the risk of surreptitious advanced transport? Because it must be hidden.  

Objections to Debater_B’s Points  
1. “Speaking Earth’s language” is at best covert; they fear exposure (“libel laws,” “tabus”).  
2. “Imported chocolate” is eaten immediately “to increase weather resistance,” not offered as surface produce. Its rarity and immediate consumption reveal a survival tactic, not hospitality.  
3. “Hiding spaceships” is understating a massive, planet-wide charade. The text never records any sighting of ships—just a fifteen-minute wait suggesting pre-landed vessels. Their whole “aboveground” existence lacks any credible transport or communication with “home.” The visitors believe they “came such a long way,” but no return flights are mentioned, because the advanced network stays hidden underground.  

Conclusion  
Every textual element—from rags, mud, and rain dances to broken speech, libel laws, and forbidden imports—shows a meticulously constructed façade of primitivism. Only by appearing helpless and undeveloped could Snaddra secure Terran aid and trade to save their dwindling world. My interpretation accounts for Skkiru’s horror at the ruse and his longing to reveal a “reasonable solution” based on genuine use of his skills underground. Debater_B’s thesis collapses under the weight of evidence of forced performance, secrecy, and the contradiction of rituals to stop rain. Therefore, the correct answer is that the Snaddrath pretended to be primitive surface-dwellers, built temporary huts and ceremonies, and rigorously suppressed any sign of their true, advanced culture.
